title: Omitted SO(5) response can repair each vector seed separately but not with one stationary coupling

claim.statement: The equal-weight response from the nine SO(5) generators orthogonal to candidate 48's residual U(1) admits a positive isotropizing weight for each seeded irrep separately, but no common weight repairs both, and the response moves the vacuum at first order.
claim.implication: A viable symmetry-restoring completion needs irrep-selective operators and a simultaneous vacuum/KKT re-solve.

setup.counterterm: lambda times sum over omitted compact generators of ||[G,Phi]||^2

interpretation: The sign is favorable: omitted SO(5) directions preferentially stiffen the light charged planes.
Different Casimir content of the 10 and 14 produces different response slopes, so one universal omitted-generator coefficient cannot cancel the same initial gap in both.
Even an irrep-specific Hessian repair is not stationary at the original vacuum without compensating deformations.
The next minimal algebraic extension is a polynomial in the completed-module SO(5) Casimir that separates eigenvalues 3/2 and 5/2, accompanied by a re-solved radial stationarity system.
falsifiers: A universal repair would require the two inferred weights to agree within numerical tolerance; they differ by 0.12294.
A fixed-vacuum repair would require zero added gradient; its norm is 9.798 per unit weight.
This no-go applies to the equal-weight nine-generator commutator response, not to general SO(5)-equivariant operators.
nextBranches: Build Casimir-polynomial projectors selecting the 10 and 14 completed-module sectors.
Solve the two-coupling seed isotropy equations and determine the compensating radial source needed for stationarity.
Test positivity on the descendant 6, 1, and 9 sectors before accepting the repair.
